raw_graphql_pull_request.body: ## Motivation Add native support for [Wan-Animate-2](https://huggingface.co/Wan-AI/Wan2.2-Animate-2-14B-Diffusers) (`Wan-AI/Wan2.2-Animate-2-14B-Diffusers`), the 14B character-animation model of the Wan2.2 family. It takes a **reference image** and a **reference video** and produces a clip of the reference subject performing the reference video's motion. Wan-Animate-2 is an in-context video model: the reference video is encoded once per clip into a K/V cache by a separate reference pass, each clip is denoised against that cache with the previous clip's last frame as conditioning, and the clips are assembled into one video. Diffusers serves it as a modular pipeline; this PR implements the model natively (`WanAnimate2Pipeline`, selected automatically from the checkpoint's `model_index.json`) and loads the same checkpoint. There is no diffusers fallback. ## Modifications ### New - `runtime/models/dits/wan_animate_2.py`, `wan_animate_2_block.py`, `wan_animate_2_clip_conditioning.py`: the in-context DiT on top of `WanTransformer3DModel`. The block runs the padded `[generation | reference-video]` layout through `torch.compile`d `flex_attention` with a per-geometry `BlockMask`; the reference K/V is computed once per clip (keys cached after RoPE) and owned by the request, the text/image context projection is computed once per clip and CFG branch, and the geometry caches hold at most four RoPE tables and two block masks. - `runtime/pipelines/wan_animate_2_pipeline.py` and `runtime/pipelines_core/stages/model_specific_stages/wan_animate_2/` (`preprocess`, `before_denoising`, `denoising`, `encoder_adapters`, `audio`): reference-video decoding (a local path, or an HTTP(S) / `data:` URL fetched through the shared media loader) and letterboxing, the three text prompts (tokenization and truncation to the DiT `text_len` live in the pipeline config), CLIP and VAE conditioning, the clip schedule, the per-clip denoise-and-decode loop, and the output stage. - `configs/models/dits/wan_animate_2.py`, `configs/pipeline_configs/wan.py` (`Wan_Animate_2_14B_Config`), `configs/sample/wan.py` (`Wan_Animate_2_14B_SamplingParam`): architecture config read from the checkpoint's `transformer/config.json` (including `text_len`, which sizes the padded prompt embedding), pipeline config with the prompt tokenization hooks and the startup validations listed below, and the model-specific sampling fields. - Cookbook page [`docs/cookbook/diffusion/Wan/Wan-Animate-2.mdx`](https://github.com/ankitdhall/sglang/blob/diffusion/wan-animate-2/docs/cookbook/diffusion/Wan/Wan-Animate-2.mdx) (serving presets, parameter reference, benchmark table), catalog entry, `docs.json`, and a note in the OpenAI API reference on the Wan-Animate-2 `size`, `seconds` and `enable_audio` semantics. - Unit tests `test/unit/test_wan_animate_2_config.py` and `test_wan_animate_2_parallelism.py`; two GPU CI cases (`wan2_2_animate_2_14b_ref2v`, 1 GPU, and `wan2_2_animate_2_14b_ref2v_cfg_parallel_2gpu`) with consistency thresholds and H100 perf scenarios (the cases run on the H100 CI lanes). ### Shared code touched - `DPMSolverMultistepScheduler.set_timesteps` accepts an explicit sigma grid (the official Wan sigma schedule is passed explicitly). - `TransformerLoader` gains a `strict_checkpoint_keys` hook; this pipeline turns it on so a checkpoint tensor that maps to no parameter fails the load (the full 1303-key mapping is pinned by a unit test). - `WanTransformer3DModel` builds its blocks through a `_make_block` factory, which the Wan-Animate-2 DiT overrides instead of rebuilding the block list. - `WanTransformerBlock` exposes its QKV projection and cross-attention/FFN tail as `_qkv` / `_cross_and_ffn`, and `WanTransformer3DModel` its output head as `_unpatchify` (method identity is pinned by a unit test). - `DenoisingStage` factors its step loop into `_run_denoising_loop` (with a `progress_step_interval` extra); `DecodingStage.decode` is split into `decode_raw` (raw `[-1, 1]` pixels) plus the `[0, 1]` normalisation. Other pipelines keep their behaviour. - The auto-residency probe fit (`gpu_worker.py`) stops when lightening a probe does not shrink it, with a regression test in `test_warmup_probe_degradation.py`: a model whose sampling params pin the frame count otherwise makes the fit loop forever on cards where the full-shape probe does not fit. ### Supported features - Server warmup (`--warmup-mode server`, and therefore `--enable-torch-compile`) with a synthetic reference image and a synthetic reference video at the default clip length, written through the shared video writer. - CFG parallelism: the conditional and unconditional branches run on separate ranks (all-gathered in branch order) and are combined with the serial `uncond + g * (cond - uncond)` arithmetic, without the shared CFG post-process; enabled automatically on 2 GPUs (the framework default, which this model keeps), forced with `--enable-cfg-parallel`, disabled with `--cfg-parallel-size 1`. With `--encoder-parallel replicate --vae-config.use-parallel-decode false` and `SGLANG_DIFFUSION_VAE_CHANNELS_LAST_3D=1` the 2-GPU output is bit-identical to the 1-GPU output. - Ulysses sequence parallelism: `--ulysses-degree N` splits attention heads across ranks with a per-block all-to-all around the compiled flex attention. `N` must divide the 40 heads. - Tensor parallelism: `--tp-size N` uses the inherited column/row-parallel layers (40 attention heads split). Recommended when the GPU has less VRAM: about 30 GiB torch peak per GPU at `--tp-size 2` (37 GiB nvidia-smi) versus 66 GiB (70 GiB) on 1 GPU. Combinable with Ulysses (`--tp-size 2 --ulysses-degree 2` on 4 GPUs; both degrees must divide the 40 heads, Ulysses the TP-local count). - Text-encoder CPU offload: `--text-encoder-cpu-offload` keeps the fp32 UMT5 encoder on the host and moves it in for each request's text encoding. Recommended when the GPU has less VRAM. - Precision: the DiT runs in bf16, the UMT5 text encoder and the CLIP image encoder in fp32; the Wan VAE encodes and decodes in fp32 with autocast off (the stage-local adapter and the clip decode pin the dtype; the configured VAE decode precision is not consulted). - DiT layerwise offload: `--dit-layerwise-offload --layerwise-offload-components transformer` streams the 40 blocks from pinned host memory with async prefetch. 1-GPU torch peak drops from 66 GiB to 37 GiB at the same end-to-end time (996 s vs 993 s in the table below). - Per-request audio: the reference video's audio track is read with the shared audio reader and carried on `OutputBatch.audio` by default, as in the official pipeline; the shared MP4 writer encodes it next to the video, as for LTX-2 and MOVA. `enable_audio=false` on a request gives a silent output. A reference video without an audio track, or one the reader cannot decode, yields a silent output with one log line per process. ### Notes on model-specific parameters - `clip_len`: the video is denoised in chunks and this is the chunk length. Must be of the form 4k+1 (VAE temporal stride 4); other values are rounded to 4k+1 with the same k and the rounding is logged (40 becomes 41, 38 and 39 become 37); values below 5 are rejected. Default: 37. - `fps`: the reference video is resampled to this rate and the output MP4 is written at this rate; duration is preserved. Default: 16. - `prompt_ref`: text for the reference-video branch; defaults to the official demo phrase "人物动作的参考视频". Recommended to leave unchanged. - `width x height` (the API's `size`): a pixel-area budget, not the output dimensions. The frame keeps the reference image's aspect ratio, rounded to multiples of 16; the letterbox bars are cropped from the output. With the default 640x800 a 9:16 reference gives a 528x944 canvas, a 1:1 reference 704x704. - `num_frames` and the API's `seconds` are not length controls: the output has as many frames as the (resampled) reference video. A supplied value is ignored and the server logs that it was. - `video_path` (or `video_url`): the reference video, a path or URL the server can read, passed as a form field or in `extra_body`; the reference image rides `input_reference`. ### Rejected at startup or request admission - `--ring-degree` greater than 1, `--use-fsdp-inference`, and TP or Ulysses degrees that do not divide the 40 attention heads (Ulysses divides the TP-local count). - An explicit `--attention-backend` (or `--component-attention-backends transformer=...`): the in-context self-attention runs on `flex_attention` only. The text encoder still accepts its own backend. - `SGLANG_DIFFUSION_ENABLE_MXFP8_ATTENTION`: this model does not apply the offline Q/K rotation. - `enable_teacache` / `enable_spectrum` request fields: every block runs at every step. - A checkpoint `transformer/config.json` with `use_img_emb=false`: the model always builds the image-embedding cross-attention, so such a checkpoint is a different model. - Any disaggregated `--disagg-role`: the per-request state crosses stages as GPU tensors and a `torch.Generator`, which the disaggregation transport cannot carry. ### Native reuse and model-specific boundaries - Text encoding uses `TextEncodingStage`; each clip uses the shared `DenoisingStage` loop, CFG utilities, profiling and component-release hooks. - QKV projections, cross-attention, FFN and output reconstruction are inherited from Wan. Ulysses uses the shared packed-QKV exchange and inverse exchange. - Clip decoding uses `DecodingStage.decode_raw`, including tiling, compile-cache management and OOM diagnostics, without converting overlap conditioning to and from [0, 1]. Thin CLIP/VAE adapters preserve the existing preprocessing and latent-scaling arithmetic; native modules remain exposed to component and layerwise-offload management. - The sequential clip schedule, reference K/V pass, in-context FlexAttention mask, branch-specific block skip and overlap-frame conditioning remain model-specific. The checkpoint scheduler uses the official explicit sigma grid per clip. Cache-dit, breakable CUDA graphs, LoRA and disaggregated serving remain unsupported; this refactor does not enable them. ## Accuracy Tests Inputs of the comparison below, identical for both frameworks. | Input 1: reference image (the subject to animate) | Input 2: reference video, 7.9 s at 30 fps (the motion to follow) | | --- | --- | | | https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/381c9204-6b60-4a50-9489-8e24000436e4 | **Output, side by side:** sglang (this PR) on the left, the diffusers 0.40 modular pipeline on the right. https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/f6200a8d-200a-42ca-ab61-d532ab82a64c **Output, frame grid at matching timestamps** (every 40th frame): sglang (this PR) top row, diffusers 0.40 bottom row. Same inputs in both frameworks: a 16:9 reference image and a 7.9 s reference video at 30 fps, `size` 640x800 (a 960x528 frame), `clip_len` 37, 40 steps, CFG 3.0, seed 123, identical prompt and negative prompt, default reference-branch prompt. sglang vs diffusers over all 237 frames: PSNR 26.14 dB mean (17.60 dB min), SSIM 0.820, LPIPS 0.127; two different seeds of diffusers are 16.69 dB / SSIM 0.49 apart, so the two frameworks sample the same point far more closely than two seeds do. The driving video is decoded on the CPU as in the reference implementation; decoding it on the GPU changes the frames and therefore the sample for a given seed. - The in-context geometry matches the diffusers reference implementation exactly where it can be checked on CPU: RoPE positions, offsets, stride and pair interleaving for the generation and reference-video grids; the block mask for every query/key pair in three clip geometries including the 128-token padding; the unconditional block-9 skip; the reference pass at timestep 1; the conditioning frame counts and mask lengths. - CFG-parallel on 2 GPUs with the three flags above is bit-identical to the 1-GPU output, so both CI cases share one ground truth per platform. Layerwise DiT offload and the standard loader path are also bit-identical to the resident single-GPU run. - The CI ground truth is generated on H100, the platform the cases run on. Frames generated on one GPU architecture differ from those of another at the independent-sample level (16 to 17 dB between H100 and GB200), so a lane on another platform would need its own frames. Both CI cases pass the harness consistency check against the H100 frames (PSNR inf, thresholds PSNR 24 dB, SSIM 0.92, CLIP 0.90); the same bit-identity holds on GB200. - `--enable-torch-compile` output lands in the known compiled-kernel band relative to eager (about 30 dB overall, worst frame about 25 dB). - Shared-code changes: the parent Wan unit tests pass unchanged, the `WanTransformer3DModel` state-dict keys are identical before and after the `_make_block` factory (pinned by a unit test), and the existing Wan2.2 TI2V-5B CI case loads and generates on this branch. How to run: ```bash # CPU unit tests (geometry, block mask, config validation, loader key mapping, probe fit) pytest python/sglang/multimodal_gen/test/unit/test_wan_animate_2_config.py \ python/sglang/multimodal_gen/test/unit/test_wan_animate_2_parallelism.py \ python/sglang/multimodal_gen/test/unit/test_warmup_probe_degradation.py # GPU CI cases (consistency against the H100 ground truth + perf check) pytest -s python/sglang/multimodal_gen/test/server/test_server_1_gpu.py -k wan2_2_animate_2_14b_ref2v pytest -s python/sglang/multimodal_gen/test/server/test_server_2_gpu.py -k wan2_2_animate_2_14b_ref2v_cfg_parallel_2gpu ``` ## Speed Tests and Profiling Tested on 1, 2 and 4 GPUs of a 4x GB200 node (189 GB per GPU). Workload: 40 steps, fps 30, 237 frames = 7 clips of 37, 640x800 budget on a 16:9 reference image (960x528 frame), CFG 3.0, seed 123, `--text-encoder-cpu-offload --warmup-mode request`. E2E is the request time with the 1-step warmup request excluded, so it excludes the one-off flex-attention compile; peak is torch reserved on rank 0 / nvidia-smi max over ranks. | Config | GPUs | Flags (plus `--text-encoder-cpu-offload`) | E2E warm (s) | Peak per GPU (GiB, torch reserved / nvidia-smi) | | --- | ---: | --- | ---: | ---: | | 1 GPU, resident | 1 | none | 993 | 66.3 / 69.5 | | 1 GPU, layerwise DiT offload | 1 | `--dit-layerwise-offload --layerwise-offload-components transformer` | 996 | 37.0 / 40.2 | | 2 GPU, CFG-parallel | 2 | `--enable-cfg-parallel` | 513 | 61.0 / 67.3 | | 2 GPU, CFG-parallel, replicated encoders + serial VAE decode | 2 | `--enable-cfg-parallel --encoder-parallel replicate --vae-config.use-parallel-decode false` | 515 | 58.5 / 71.0 | | 2 GPU, CFG-parallel, layerwise DiT offload (CI configuration, bit-identical to 1 GPU) | 2 | `--enable-cfg-parallel --dit-layerwise-offload --layerwise-offload-components transformer --encoder-parallel replicate --vae-config.use-parallel-decode false` + `SGLANG_DIFFUSION_VAE_CHANNELS_LAST_3D=1` | 512 | 29.9 / 43.0 | | 2 GPU, Ulysses2 | 2 | `--ulysses-degree 2` | 547 | 49.0 / 58.1 | | 2 GPU, TP2 | 2 | `--tp-size 2` | 613 | 29.8 / 36.6 | | 4 GPU, auto default (CFG2 x SP2, KV-gather exchange) | 4 | none | 283 | 48.4 / 58.4 | | 4 GPU, CFG2 x Ulysses2 | 4 | `--enable-cfg-parallel --ulysses-degree 2` | 283 | 48.5 / 58.4 | | 4 GPU, CFG2 x Ulysses2, replicated encoders, serial VAE decode | 4 | `--enable-cfg-parallel --ulysses-degree 2 --encoder-parallel replicate --vae-config.use-parallel-decode false` | 287 | 53.4 / 62.5 | | 4 GPU, CFG2 x Ulysses2, layerwise DiT offload | 4 | `--enable-cfg-parallel --ulysses-degree 2 --dit-layerwise-offload --layerwise-offload-components transformer --encoder-parallel replicate --vae-config.use-parallel-decode false` | 291 | 22.1 / 35.2 | | 4 GPU, Ulysses4 | 4 | `--ulysses-degree 4` | 317 | 40.0 / 49.0 | | 4 GPU, CFG2 x TP2 | 4 | `--enable-cfg-parallel --tp-size 2` | 318 | 30.1 / 37.5 | | 4 GPU, TP2 x Ulysses2 | 4 | `--tp-size 2 --ulysses-degree 2` | 361 | 25.1 / 33.5 | | 4 GPU, TP4 | 4 | `--tp-size 4` | 379 | 21.6 / 27.3 | | diffusers 0.40.0 modular, 1 GPU, `compile_repeated_blocks` | 1 | n/a | 978 (cold 1004) | 71.3 reserved | Speedups: 4 GPUs are 3.5x over 1 GPU (283 s vs 993 s) and 3.5x over diffusers, which has no multi-GPU path for this model; 2 GPUs are 1.9x with CFG-parallel and 1.8x with Ulysses, 1.6x with TP2. Among 4-GPU layouts the framework default and the explicit CFG2 x Ulysses2 exchange run at the same speed (283 s); CFG2 x TP2 and Ulysses4 are both about 12 percent slower at 18 and 8 GB less torch peak; TP4 is 34 percent slower for the lowest footprint (22 GB torch, 27 GB nvidia-smi). TP2 x Ulysses2 is the memory-leaning layout after TP4 (25 GB torch, 33 GB nvidia-smi), about 13 percent slower than CFG2 x TP2 and 27 percent slower than the default. CI perf scenarios (8 steps, one 29-frame clip, 576x1024, layerwise DiT, warmup active) on the H100 80 GB lanes: 98.4 s end-to-end on 1 GPU and 64.0 s on 2 GPUs CFG-parallel, average denoising step 10.8 s and 6.4 s, peak 35.5 GiB (36,322 MiB) on both. Both cases run with the per-step and VRAM perf validation enabled (`run_perf_check=True`). ### Recommended parallelism config It is recommended to use `--text-encoder-cpu-offload`. **1 GPU** - 96 GB or more: defaults (DiT resident, 66 GiB torch peak, 70 GiB nvidia-smi). - 80 GB: add `--dit-layerwise-offload --layerwise-offload-components transformer` (37 GiB torch peak, 40 GiB nvidia-smi, same end-to-end time). **2 GPUs** - `--enable-cfg-parallel --encoder-parallel replicate --vae-config.use-parallel-decode false` with `SGLANG_DIFFUSION_VAE_CHANNELS_LAST_3D=1`: the 2-GPU recipe whose output is bit-identical to 1 GPU: 515 s, 59 GiB torch peak (71 GiB nvidia-smi) per GPU, the same speed as plain CFG-parallel (513 s). - 80 GB or less per GPU: the same CFG-parallel recipe with `--dit-layerwise-offload --layerwise-offload-components transformer` (512 s, 30 GiB torch peak, 43 GiB nvidia-smi, still bit-identical), or `--tp-size 2` (613 s, 30 GiB torch peak, 37 GiB nvidia-smi). **4 GPUs** - `--enable-cfg-parallel --ulysses-degree 2`: 3.5x over 1 GPU (283 s), 48 GiB torch peak per GPU (58 GiB nvidia-smi). Ulysses shards the attention sequence, so no 4-GPU layout is bit-identical to a single GPU; they match the single-GPU video to about 30 dB mean PSNR, with or without `--encoder-parallel replicate --vae-config.use-parallel-decode false` (287 s, 53 GiB torch peak). The 4-GPU framework default (CFG2 x SP2 with the KV-gather exchange) runs at the same speed and produces the same output, but pass `--enable-cfg-parallel --ulysses-degree 2` explicitly: it pins the layout the 80 GB row was measured on. - 80 GB or less per GPU: the same CFG-parallel x Ulysses recipe with `--dit-layerwise-offload --layerwise-offload-components transformer` (291 s, 22 GiB torch peak, 35 GiB nvidia-smi), or `--enable-cfg-parallel --tp-size 2` (318 s, 30 GiB torch peak, 37 GiB nvidia-smi). - Memory-leaning: `--tp-size 2 --ulysses-degree 2` (361 s, 25 GiB torch peak, 33 GiB nvidia-smi), the lowest 4-GPU peak after `--tp-size 4`, about 13 percent slower than CFG2 x TP2 and 27 percent slower than CFG2 x Ulysses2; use the default for speed and this layout for memory. The two extra flags `--encoder-parallel replicate --vae-config.use-parallel-decode false` keep the encoders whole on every rank and decode the VAE on one rank. ## Known limitations and follow-ups - The distilled checkpoint (`Wan-AI/Wan2.2-Animate-2-14B-Distilled-Diffusers`, 10 steps, no CFG) is not supported in this PR (a follow-up PR adds it). The DiT reads `log_scale` from the checkpoint's `transformer/config.json`; the released base config has no such key and the attention score modifier is an exact identity at 0. - Ring attention is not implemented: the in-context block mask needs the full K/V on one rank. - Quantization, TeaCache / cache-dit and LoRA are not supported: the MXFP8 attention path and the `enable_teacache` / `enable_spectrum` request fields are rejected as listed above, and no LoRA or other quantized path is wired for this pipeline. Disaggregated serving is rejected. ### Resolved known limitations - [x] `--tp-size` combined with `--ulysses-degree` was rejected because of an upstream Wan VAE encoder issue; the fix landed in #41917, so the rejection is lifted and the TP2 x Ulysses2 layout is benchmarked in the table above and in the cookbook. - [x] The two CI cases read their inputs and ground-truth frames from sgl-project/ci-data-diffusion at the `main` commit pinned by `SGL_TEST_FILES_CI_DATA_REVISION`; the H100 frames are the ones the CI run generated and the maintainer committed from it. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [x] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): :white_check_mark: [Run #37917459115](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/37917459115) Latest PR Test (Extra): :x: [Run #37917458682](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/37917458682) Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 10): :hourglass_flowing_sand: [Run #37917459035](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/37917459035)

nodes.body: Pushed another native-reuse pass in a25e932d4aa3: shared Wan QKV/cross-attention/FFN/output head, shared packed Ulysses exchange, and raw clip decoding through DecodingStage. Production code is 40 lines smaller. 165 tests pass; actual two-GPU exchanges and small native Wan block/VAE comparisons are bit-identical. Kept the model-specific RoPE: the generic FMA kernel changes rounding. Full 14B e2e has not been rerun for this commit.

The remaining Wan CFG2 consistency failure also reproduces on a single Hopper GPU. I compared the original PR at 1d582a46f77 with the repaired head on H200: reference VAE output, initial noise, first prediction, final latents, decoded pixels and all 24 frames are bit-identical. The same full-model comparison passes on B200, including single-GPU vs CFG2. Could you share the exact source SHA, generation command, model revision and package versions used for ci-data-diffusion#12? The GT currently has no generation manifest, so I do not want to replace it with the failing CI output without explaining the mismatch.

Pushed aa70506ab73 (20 added lines, 2 removed). The two NVFP4 startup failures were caused by WanAnimate2TransformerLoader inheriting component_names and replacing the shared transformer loader globally; it is now pipeline-local, with a registration regression test. 142 focused tests pass, and Wan NVFP4 passes the real B200 server case. Ideogram independently hits a gated-HF 401 on the devbox, so its e2e rerun remains unverified. The H3 5090 failure used an 8-update GT from unmerged #38671 against main’s 7-update path. Restored the compatible H3 GT while retaining the Wan assets; all three actual CI artifact frames now pass unchanged thresholds (minimum SSIM 0.9258, minimum PSNR 36.20, maximum MAE 2.62). New-head CI is queued. Wan GT remains unchanged pending provenance; the one cold-load failure passed on retry (106.06s -> 31.13s), so I have not relaxed its performance threshold.

Fixed the unit-test failure in fb9866f7366b. The 16x16 MP4 fixture reproduces decord’s RGB buffer-size mismatch (1536 vs 768); our previous dev environment used the PyAV fallback and missed it. The fixture now uses aligned 32x64 frames, with an explicit resampled shape assertion. Real local-file/URL decoding and pixel equality are still checked. All 142 focused Wan tests pass with decord 0.6.0; the target test also passes with PyAV. Pre-commit passes. No production code or thresholds changed.

Refreshed the six H100 Wan Animate reference frames from run 37889108770 artifacts (single-GPU and CFG2). All three RGB frames are bit-identical between these configurations, and all six published files were read back from the pinned revision and verified byte-for-byte. ci-data main: 31d8ad69f2434727aad518f0678fbd57823856fe; PR pin update: 451545da69ed. Thresholds and other models GT are unchanged. Added source manifests. This establishes the current CI output as the regression baseline; the original GT generation mismatch remains unexplained and this is not a claim of official numerical parity. Pre-commit passes.

Updated the PR description and the cookbook with fresh performance numbers: 3-7% faster and 1-13 GB lower max VRAM.

Closing https://github.com/sgl-project/ci-data-diffusion/pull/12 in favour of https://github.com/sgl-project/ci-data-diffusion/commit/31d8ad69f2434727aad518f0678fbd57823856fe

detail.body: ## Motivation Add native support for [Wan-Animate-2](https://huggingface.co/Wan-AI/Wan2.2-Animate-2-14B-Diffusers) (`Wan-AI/Wan2.2-Animate-2-14B-Diffusers`), the 14B character-animation model of the Wan2.2 family. It takes a **reference image** and a **reference video** and produces a clip of the reference subject performing the reference video's motion. Wan-Animate-2 is an in-context video model: the reference video is encoded once per clip into a K/V cache by a separate reference pass, each clip is denoised against that cache with the previous clip's last frame as conditioning, and the clips are assembled into one video. Diffusers serves it as a modular pipeline; this PR implements the model natively (`WanAnimate2Pipeline`, selected automatically from the checkpoint's `model_index.json`) and loads the same checkpoint. There is no diffusers fallback. ## Modifications ### New - `runtime/models/dits/wan_animate_2.py`, `wan_animate_2_block.py`, `wan_animate_2_clip_conditioning.py`: the in-context DiT on top of `WanTransformer3DModel`. The block runs the padded `[generation | reference-video]` layout through `torch.compile`d `flex_attention` with a per-geometry `BlockMask`; the reference K/V is computed once per clip (keys cached after RoPE) and owned by the request, the text/image context projection is computed once per clip and CFG branch, and the geometry caches hold at most four RoPE tables and two block masks. - `runtime/pipelines/wan_animate_2_pipeline.py` and `runtime/pipelines_core/stages/model_specific_stages/wan_animate_2/` (`preprocess`, `before_denoising`, `denoising`, `encoder_adapters`, `audio`): reference-video decoding (a local path, or an HTTP(S) / `data:` URL fetched through the shared media loader) and letterboxing, the three text prompts (tokenization and truncation to the DiT `text_len` live in the pipeline config), CLIP and VAE conditioning, the clip schedule, the per-clip denoise-and-decode loop, and the output stage. - `configs/models/dits/wan_animate_2.py`, `configs/pipeline_configs/wan.py` (`Wan_Animate_2_14B_Config`), `configs/sample/wan.py` (`Wan_Animate_2_14B_SamplingParam`): architecture config read from the checkpoint's `transformer/config.json` (including `text_len`, which sizes the padded prompt embedding), pipeline config with the prompt tokenization hooks and the startup validations listed below, and the model-specific sampling fields. - Cookbook page [`docs/cookbook/diffusion/Wan/Wan-Animate-2.mdx`](https://github.com/ankitdhall/sglang/blob/diffusion/wan-animate-2/docs/cookbook/diffusion/Wan/Wan-Animate-2.mdx) (serving presets, parameter reference, benchmark table), catalog entry, `docs.json`, and a note in the OpenAI API reference on the Wan-Animate-2 `size`, `seconds` and `enable_audio` semantics. - Unit tests `test/unit/test_wan_animate_2_config.py` and `test_wan_animate_2_parallelism.py`; two GPU CI cases (`wan2_2_animate_2_14b_ref2v`, 1 GPU, and `wan2_2_animate_2_14b_ref2v_cfg_parallel_2gpu`) with consistency thresholds and H100 perf scenarios (the cases run on the H100 CI lanes). ### Shared code touched - `DPMSolverMultistepScheduler.set_timesteps` accepts an explicit sigma grid (the official Wan sigma schedule is passed explicitly). - `TransformerLoader` gains a `strict_checkpoint_keys` hook; this pipeline turns it on so a checkpoint tensor that maps to no parameter fails the load (the full 1303-key mapping is pinned by a unit test). - `WanTransformer3DModel` builds its blocks through a `_make_block` factory, which the Wan-Animate-2 DiT overrides instead of rebuilding the block list. - `WanTransformerBlock` exposes its QKV projection and cross-attention/FFN tail as `_qkv` / `_cross_and_ffn`, and `WanTransformer3DModel` its output head as `_unpatchify` (method identity is pinned by a unit test). - `DenoisingStage` factors its step loop into `_run_denoising_loop` (with a `progress_step_interval` extra); `DecodingStage.decode` is split into `decode_raw` (raw `[-1, 1]` pixels) plus the `[0, 1]` normalisation. Other pipelines keep their behaviour. - The auto-residency probe fit (`gpu_worker.py`) stops when lightening a probe does not shrink it, with a regression test in `test_warmup_probe_degradation.py`: a model whose sampling params pin the frame count otherwise makes the fit loop forever on cards where the full-shape probe does not fit. ### Supported features - Server warmup (`--warmup-mode server`, and therefore `--enable-torch-compile`) with a synthetic reference image and a synthetic reference video at the default clip length, written through the shared video writer. - CFG parallelism: the conditional and unconditional branches run on separate ranks (all-gathered in branch order) and are combined with the serial `uncond + g * (cond - uncond)` arithmetic, without the shared CFG post-process; enabled automatically on 2 GPUs (the framework default, which this model keeps), forced with `--enable-cfg-parallel`, disabled with `--cfg-parallel-size 1`. With `--encoder-parallel replicate --vae-config.use-parallel-decode false` and `SGLANG_DIFFUSION_VAE_CHANNELS_LAST_3D=1` the 2-GPU output is bit-identical to the 1-GPU output. - Ulysses sequence parallelism: `--ulysses-degree N` splits attention heads across ranks with a per-block all-to-all around the compiled flex attention. `N` must divide the 40 heads. - Tensor parallelism: `--tp-size N` uses the inherited column/row-parallel layers (40 attention heads split). Recommended when the GPU has less VRAM: about 30 GiB torch peak per GPU at `--tp-size 2` (37 GiB nvidia-smi) versus 66 GiB (70 GiB) on 1 GPU. Combinable with Ulysses (`--tp-size 2 --ulysses-degree 2` on 4 GPUs; both degrees must divide the 40 heads, Ulysses the TP-local count). - Text-encoder CPU offload: `--text-encoder-cpu-offload` keeps the fp32 UMT5 encoder on the host and moves it in for each request's text encoding. Recommended when the GPU has less VRAM. - Precision: the DiT runs in bf16, the UMT5 text encoder and the CLIP image encoder in fp32; the Wan VAE encodes and decodes in fp32 with autocast off (the stage-local adapter and the clip decode pin the dtype; the configured VAE decode precision is not consulted). - DiT layerwise offload: `--dit-layerwise-offload --layerwise-offload-components transformer` streams the 40 blocks from pinned host memory with async prefetch. 1-GPU torch peak drops from 66 GiB to 37 GiB at the same end-to-end time (996 s vs 993 s in the table below). - Per-request audio: the reference video's audio track is read with the shared audio reader and carried on `OutputBatch.audio` by default, as in the official pipeline; the shared MP4 writer encodes it next to the video, as for LTX-2 and MOVA. `enable_audio=false` on a request gives a silent output. A reference video without an audio track, or one the reader cannot decode, yields a silent output with one log line per process. ### Notes on model-specific parameters - `clip_len`: the video is denoised in chunks and this is the chunk length. Must be of the form 4k+1 (VAE temporal stride 4); other values are rounded to 4k+1 with the same k and the rounding is logged (40 becomes 41, 38 and 39 become 37); values below 5 are rejected. Default: 37. - `fps`: the reference video is resampled to this rate and the output MP4 is written at this rate; duration is preserved. Default: 16. - `prompt_ref`: text for the reference-video branch; defaults to the official demo phrase "人物动作的参考视频". Recommended to leave unchanged. - `width x height` (the API's `size`): a pixel-area budget, not the output dimensions. The frame keeps the reference image's aspect ratio, rounded to multiples of 16; the letterbox bars are cropped from the output. With the default 640x800 a 9:16 reference gives a 528x944 canvas, a 1:1 reference 704x704. - `num_frames` and the API's `seconds` are not length controls: the output has as many frames as the (resampled) reference video. A supplied value is ignored and the server logs that it was. - `video_path` (or `video_url`): the reference video, a path or URL the server can read, passed as a form field or in `extra_body`; the reference image rides `input_reference`. ### Rejected at startup or request admission - `--ring-degree` greater than 1, `--use-fsdp-inference`, and TP or Ulysses degrees that do not divide the 40 attention heads (Ulysses divides the TP-local count). - An explicit `--attention-backend` (or `--component-attention-backends transformer=...`): the in-context self-attention runs on `flex_attention` only. The text encoder still accepts its own backend. - `SGLANG_DIFFUSION_ENABLE_MXFP8_ATTENTION`: this model does not apply the offline Q/K rotation. - `enable_teacache` / `enable_spectrum` request fields: every block runs at every step. - A checkpoint `transformer/config.json` with `use_img_emb=false`: the model always builds the image-embedding cross-attention, so such a checkpoint is a different model. - Any disaggregated `--disagg-role`: the per-request state crosses stages as GPU tensors and a `torch.Generator`, which the disaggregation transport cannot carry. ### Native reuse and model-specific boundaries - Text encoding uses `TextEncodingStage`; each clip uses the shared `DenoisingStage` loop, CFG utilities, profiling and component-release hooks. - QKV projections, cross-attention, FFN and output reconstruction are inherited from Wan. Ulysses uses the shared packed-QKV exchange and inverse exchange. - Clip decoding uses `DecodingStage.decode_raw`, including tiling, compile-cache management and OOM diagnostics, without converting overlap conditioning to and from [0, 1]. Thin CLIP/VAE adapters preserve the existing preprocessing and latent-scaling arithmetic; native modules remain exposed to component and layerwise-offload management. - The sequential clip schedule, reference K/V pass, in-context FlexAttention mask, branch-specific block skip and overlap-frame conditioning remain model-specific. The checkpoint scheduler uses the official explicit sigma grid per clip. Cache-dit, breakable CUDA graphs, LoRA and disaggregated serving remain unsupported; this refactor does not enable them. ## Accuracy Tests Inputs of the comparison below, identical for both frameworks. | Input 1: reference image (the subject to animate) | Input 2: reference video, 7.9 s at 30 fps (the motion to follow) | | --- | --- | | | https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/381c9204-6b60-4a50-9489-8e24000436e4 | **Output, side by side:** sglang (this PR) on the left, the diffusers 0.40 modular pipeline on the right. https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/f6200a8d-200a-42ca-ab61-d532ab82a64c **Output, frame grid at matching timestamps** (every 40th frame): sglang (this PR) top row, diffusers 0.40 bottom row. Same inputs in both frameworks: a 16:9 reference image and a 7.9 s reference video at 30 fps, `size` 640x800 (a 960x528 frame), `clip_len` 37, 40 steps, CFG 3.0, seed 123, identical prompt and negative prompt, default reference-branch prompt. sglang vs diffusers over all 237 frames: PSNR 26.14 dB mean (17.60 dB min), SSIM 0.820, LPIPS 0.127; two different seeds of diffusers are 16.69 dB / SSIM 0.49 apart, so the two frameworks sample the same point far more closely than two seeds do. The driving video is decoded on the CPU as in the reference implementation; decoding it on the GPU changes the frames and therefore the sample for a given seed. - The in-context geometry matches the diffusers reference implementation exactly where it can be checked on CPU: RoPE positions, offsets, stride and pair interleaving for the generation and reference-video grids; the block mask for every query/key pair in three clip geometries including the 128-token padding; the unconditional block-9 skip; the reference pass at timestep 1; the conditioning frame counts and mask lengths. - CFG-parallel on 2 GPUs with the three flags above is bit-identical to the 1-GPU output, so both CI cases share one ground truth per platform. Layerwise DiT offload and the standard loader path are also bit-identical to the resident single-GPU run. - The CI ground truth is generated on H100, the platform the cases run on. Frames generated on one GPU architecture differ from those of another at the independent-sample level (16 to 17 dB between H100 and GB200), so a lane on another platform would need its own frames. Both CI cases pass the harness consistency check against the H100 frames (PSNR inf, thresholds PSNR 24 dB, SSIM 0.92, CLIP 0.90); the same bit-identity holds on GB200. - `--enable-torch-compile` output lands in the known compiled-kernel band relative to eager (about 30 dB overall, worst frame about 25 dB). - Shared-code changes: the parent Wan unit tests pass unchanged, the `WanTransformer3DModel` state-dict keys are identical before and after the `_make_block` factory (pinned by a unit test), and the existing Wan2.2 TI2V-5B CI case loads and generates on this branch. How to run: ```bash # CPU unit tests (geometry, block mask, config validation, loader key mapping, probe fit) pytest python/sglang/multimodal_gen/test/unit/test_wan_animate_2_config.py \ python/sglang/multimodal_gen/test/unit/test_wan_animate_2_parallelism.py \ python/sglang/multimodal_gen/test/unit/test_warmup_probe_degradation.py # GPU CI cases (consistency against the H100 ground truth + perf check) pytest -s python/sglang/multimodal_gen/test/server/test_server_1_gpu.py -k wan2_2_animate_2_14b_ref2v pytest -s python/sglang/multimodal_gen/test/server/test_server_2_gpu.py -k wan2_2_animate_2_14b_ref2v_cfg_parallel_2gpu ``` ## Speed Tests and Profiling Tested on 1, 2 and 4 GPUs of a 4x GB200 node (189 GB per GPU). Workload: 40 steps, fps 30, 237 frames = 7 clips of 37, 640x800 budget on a 16:9 reference image (960x528 frame), CFG 3.0, seed 123, `--text-encoder-cpu-offload --warmup-mode request`. E2E is the request time with the 1-step warmup request excluded, so it excludes the one-off flex-attention compile; peak is torch reserved on rank 0 / nvidia-smi max over ranks. | Config | GPUs | Flags (plus `--text-encoder-cpu-offload`) | E2E warm (s) | Peak per GPU (GiB, torch reserved / nvidia-smi) | | --- | ---: | --- | ---: | ---: | | 1 GPU, resident | 1 | none | 993 | 66.3 / 69.5 | | 1 GPU, layerwise DiT offload | 1 | `--dit-layerwise-offload --layerwise-offload-components transformer` | 996 | 37.0 / 40.2 | | 2 GPU, CFG-parallel | 2 | `--enable-cfg-parallel` | 513 | 61.0 / 67.3 | | 2 GPU, CFG-parallel, replicated encoders + serial VAE decode | 2 | `--enable-cfg-parallel --encoder-parallel replicate --vae-config.use-parallel-decode false` | 515 | 58.5 / 71.0 | | 2 GPU, CFG-parallel, layerwise DiT offload (CI configuration, bit-identical to 1 GPU) | 2 | `--enable-cfg-parallel --dit-layerwise-offload --layerwise-offload-components transformer --encoder-parallel replicate --vae-config.use-parallel-decode false` + `SGLANG_DIFFUSION_VAE_CHANNELS_LAST_3D=1` | 512 | 29.9 / 43.0 | | 2 GPU, Ulysses2 | 2 | `--ulysses-degree 2` | 547 | 49.0 / 58.1 | | 2 GPU, TP2 | 2 | `--tp-size 2` | 613 | 29.8 / 36.6 | | 4 GPU, auto default (CFG2 x SP2, KV-gather exchange) | 4 | none | 283 | 48.4 / 58.4 | | 4 GPU, CFG2 x Ulysses2 | 4 | `--enable-cfg-parallel --ulysses-degree 2` | 283 | 48.5 / 58.4 | | 4 GPU, CFG2 x Ulysses2, replicated encoders, serial VAE decode | 4 | `--enable-cfg-parallel --ulysses-degree 2 --encoder-parallel replicate --vae-config.use-parallel-decode false` | 287 | 53.4 / 62.5 | | 4 GPU, CFG2 x Ulysses2, layerwise DiT offload | 4 | `--enable-cfg-parallel --ulysses-degree 2 --dit-layerwise-offload --layerwise-offload-components transformer --encoder-parallel replicate --vae-config.use-parallel-decode false` | 291 | 22.1 / 35.2 | | 4 GPU, Ulysses4 | 4 | `--ulysses-degree 4` | 317 | 40.0 / 49.0 | | 4 GPU, CFG2 x TP2 | 4 | `--enable-cfg-parallel --tp-size 2` | 318 | 30.1 / 37.5 | | 4 GPU, TP2 x Ulysses2 | 4 | `--tp-size 2 --ulysses-degree 2` | 361 | 25.1 / 33.5 | | 4 GPU, TP4 | 4 | `--tp-size 4` | 379 | 21.6 / 27.3 | | diffusers 0.40.0 modular, 1 GPU, `compile_repeated_blocks` | 1 | n/a | 978 (cold 1004) | 71.3 reserved | Speedups: 4 GPUs are 3.5x over 1 GPU (283 s vs 993 s) and 3.5x over diffusers, which has no multi-GPU path for this model; 2 GPUs are 1.9x with CFG-parallel and 1.8x with Ulysses, 1.6x with TP2. Among 4-GPU layouts the framework default and the explicit CFG2 x Ulysses2 exchange run at the same speed (283 s); CFG2 x TP2 and Ulysses4 are both about 12 percent slower at 18 and 8 GB less torch peak; TP4 is 34 percent slower for the lowest footprint (22 GB torch, 27 GB nvidia-smi). TP2 x Ulysses2 is the memory-leaning layout after TP4 (25 GB torch, 33 GB nvidia-smi), about 13 percent slower than CFG2 x TP2 and 27 percent slower than the default. CI perf scenarios (8 steps, one 29-frame clip, 576x1024, layerwise DiT, warmup active) on the H100 80 GB lanes: 98.4 s end-to-end on 1 GPU and 64.0 s on 2 GPUs CFG-parallel, average denoising step 10.8 s and 6.4 s, peak 35.5 GiB (36,322 MiB) on both. Both cases run with the per-step and VRAM perf validation enabled (`run_perf_check=True`). ### Recommended parallelism config It is recommended to use `--text-encoder-cpu-offload`. **1 GPU** - 96 GB or more: defaults (DiT resident, 66 GiB torch peak, 70 GiB nvidia-smi). - 80 GB: add `--dit-layerwise-offload --layerwise-offload-components transformer` (37 GiB torch peak, 40 GiB nvidia-smi, same end-to-end time). **2 GPUs** - `--enable-cfg-parallel --encoder-parallel replicate --vae-config.use-parallel-decode false` with `SGLANG_DIFFUSION_VAE_CHANNELS_LAST_3D=1`: the 2-GPU recipe whose output is bit-identical to 1 GPU: 515 s, 59 GiB torch peak (71 GiB nvidia-smi) per GPU, the same speed as plain CFG-parallel (513 s). - 80 GB or less per GPU: the same CFG-parallel recipe with `--dit-layerwise-offload --layerwise-offload-components transformer` (512 s, 30 GiB torch peak, 43 GiB nvidia-smi, still bit-identical), or `--tp-size 2` (613 s, 30 GiB torch peak, 37 GiB nvidia-smi). **4 GPUs** - `--enable-cfg-parallel --ulysses-degree 2`: 3.5x over 1 GPU (283 s), 48 GiB torch peak per GPU (58 GiB nvidia-smi). Ulysses shards the attention sequence, so no 4-GPU layout is bit-identical to a single GPU; they match the single-GPU video to about 30 dB mean PSNR, with or without `--encoder-parallel replicate --vae-config.use-parallel-decode false` (287 s, 53 GiB torch peak). The 4-GPU framework default (CFG2 x SP2 with the KV-gather exchange) runs at the same speed and produces the same output, but pass `--enable-cfg-parallel --ulysses-degree 2` explicitly: it pins the layout the 80 GB row was measured on. - 80 GB or less per GPU: the same CFG-parallel x Ulysses recipe with `--dit-layerwise-offload --layerwise-offload-components transformer` (291 s, 22 GiB torch peak, 35 GiB nvidia-smi), or `--enable-cfg-parallel --tp-size 2` (318 s, 30 GiB torch peak, 37 GiB nvidia-smi). - Memory-leaning: `--tp-size 2 --ulysses-degree 2` (361 s, 25 GiB torch peak, 33 GiB nvidia-smi), the lowest 4-GPU peak after `--tp-size 4`, about 13 percent slower than CFG2 x TP2 and 27 percent slower than CFG2 x Ulysses2; use the default for speed and this layout for memory. The two extra flags `--encoder-parallel replicate --vae-config.use-parallel-decode false` keep the encoders whole on every rank and decode the VAE on one rank. ## Known limitations and follow-ups - The distilled checkpoint (`Wan-AI/Wan2.2-Animate-2-14B-Distilled-Diffusers`, 10 steps, no CFG) is not supported in this PR (a follow-up PR adds it). The DiT reads `log_scale` from the checkpoint's `transformer/config.json`; the released base config has no such key and the attention score modifier is an exact identity at 0. - Ring attention is not implemented: the in-context block mask needs the full K/V on one rank. - Quantization, TeaCache / cache-dit and LoRA are not supported: the MXFP8 attention path and the `enable_teacache` / `enable_spectrum` request fields are rejected as listed above, and no LoRA or other quantized path is wired for this pipeline. Disaggregated serving is rejected. ### Resolved known limitations - [x] `--tp-size` combined with `--ulysses-degree` was rejected because of an upstream Wan VAE encoder issue; the fix landed in #41917, so the rejection is lifted and the TP2 x Ulysses2 layout is benchmarked in the table above and in the cookbook. - [x] The two CI cases read their inputs and ground-truth frames from sgl-project/ci-data-diffusion at the `main` commit pinned by `SGL_TEST_FILES_CI_DATA_REVISION`; the H100 frames are the ones the CI run generated and the maintainer committed from it. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [x] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): :white_check_mark: [Run #37917459115](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/37917459115) Latest PR Test (Extra): :x: [Run #37917458682](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/37917458682) Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 10): :hourglass_flowing_sand: [Run #37917459035](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/37917459035)
detail.title: [diffusion] model: support Wan-Animate-2

files.patch:
@@ -0,0 +1,377 @@
+---
+title: Wan-Animate-2
+description: Run Wan-Animate-2 character animation (reference image + reference video) with SGLang Diffusion.
+metatags:
+    description: "Deploy and use the Wan2.2-Animate-2 14B character-animation model with SGLang Diffusion: reference-image + reference-video conditioning, single-expert native pipeline, config-file and /v1/videos invocation, and multi-GPU presets."
+---
+
+import { DiffusionModelTags } from '/src/snippets/diffusion/model-tags.jsx';
+
+<DiffusionModelTags tags={["video", "character animation", "image + reference video", "single-expert", "640×800 / 720×1280"]} />
+
+## 1. Model Introduction
+
+[Wan-Animate-2](https://huggingface.co/Wan-AI/Wan2.2-Animate-2-14B-Diffusers) is a
+14B character-animation model in the Wan2.2 family. Instead of the text- or
+image-only conditioning of the other Wan2.2 checkpoints, it animates a **reference
+image** so that it follows the motion of a **reference video**, producing a new clip
+of that subject performing the reference video's motion.
+
+Use **`Wan-AI/Wan2.2-Animate-2-14B-Diffusers`** as `--model-path`. The distilled
+checkpoint (`Wan-AI/Wan2.2-Animate-2-14B-Distilled-Diffusers`, `log_scale=-1.3`,
+10 steps, no CFG) is not supported in this release.
+
+Unlike the A14B T2V/I2V checkpoints, Wan-Animate-2 is a **single-expert** model:
+it has one `guidance_scale` (default `3.0`), no low-noise expert
+(`guidance_scale_2`) and no boundary switching. Diffusers >= 0.40.0 serves
+Wan-Animate-2 as a modular pipeline (`WanAnimate2ModularPipeline`); SGLang
+implements the model natively and loads the same
+`Wan-AI/Wan2.2-Animate-2-14B-Diffusers` checkpoint. There is no diffusers backend
+fallback.
+
+<Warning>
+Wan-Animate-2 is served through the native `WanAnimate2Pipeline`, selected
+automatically from the checkpoint's `model_index.json`. It takes **two** inputs, a
+reference image and a reference video, so it is invoked differently from the
+other Wan2.2 models. See [section 4](#4-model-invocation).
+</Warning>
+
+### 1.1 Inputs
+
+| Input | Field | Passed via |
+| --- | --- | --- |
+| Reference image (the subject to animate) | `image_path` / `input_reference` | `--config` YAML for `sglang generate`; the `input_reference` part of a `POST /v1/videos` request |
+| Reference video (the motion to follow) | `video_path` | `--video-path` or `--config` YAML for `sglang generate`; the `video_path` field in the `/v1/videos` request body or `extra_body` |
+
+Both inputs are the base `image_path` / `video_path` sampling fields shared with the
+other video models; Wan-Animate-2 adds no model-specific input field. Offline runs
+pass both through a `--config` file (or `--image-path` / `--video-path`), and the
+online API forwards `video_path` into the pipeline while the reference image rides
+`input_reference`. Local paths must be readable by the server process. HTTP(S)
+video URLs use SGLang's shared media loader before decoding, without a disk cache.
+
+### 1.2 Defaults
+
+| Parameter | Default | Notes |
+| --- | --- | --- |
+| Resolution (`width`×`height`, the API's `size`) | `640`×`800` | A pixel-area budget, not the output dimensions: the frame keeps the reference image's aspect ratio and is the largest 16-aligned canvas with at most `width × height` pixels (see **Output resolution** below). `720`×`1280` is the larger supported budget. |
+| `clip_len` | `37` | Per-clip denoising chunk length; must be `4k+1` (VAE temporal stride 4), e.g. `37`, `65`, `81`. Other values are rounded to `4k+1` with the same `k` and the rounding is logged (`40` becomes `41`; `38` and `39` become `37`); values below `5` are rejected. |
+| `fps` | `16` | The reference video is resampled to this rate and the output MP4 is written at it; duration is preserved. |
+| `num_inference_steps` | `40` | Fewer steps (e.g. `20`) run faster. |
+| `guidance_scale` | `3.0` | Single expert; there is no `guidance_scale_2`. |
+| `prompt_ref` | `人物动作的参考视频` ("reference video of the character's motion") | Text for the reference-video branch. The official demo conditions that branch on this fixed description of the reference video rather than on the scene prompt; leave it unchanged unless reproducing a different reference setup. |
+| `enable_audio` | `true` | Keep the reference video's audio track on the output (see **Audio** below). Per request, like `clip_len`. |
+
+**Output length.** The output has as many frames as the (resampled) reference
+video, not `clip_len`. The video is generated clip by clip with `clip_len` frames
+per chunk; a larger `clip_len` improves temporal coherence at the cost of VRAM.
+`clip_len=81` roughly doubles the attention tokens of the default and OOMs a
+single 80 GB GPU. `num_frames` (and the API's `seconds`, which maps to it) does
+not control the length: it is ignored and the server logs that it was, so leave
+it unset.
+
+**Output resolution.** `width`×`height` (the API's `size`) is a pixel-area budget,
+not the output dimensions. The reference image's aspect ratio is kept, the frame is
+the largest canvas with at most `width × height` pixels whose sides are multiples of
+16, and the reference image and the driving-video frames are letterboxed onto it;
+the output MP4 has the canvas size. At the default `640`×`800` (512,000 pixels) a
+9:16 reference gives `528`×`944`, a 1:1 reference gives `704`×`704`, and only a 4:5
+reference gives exactly `640`×`800`. To obtain a specific output size, request a
+budget with the same aspect ratio as the reference image (for a 9:16 image,
+`576`×`1024` maps onto itself). This differs from the OpenAI Videos API and from the
+other SGLang diffusion pipelines, where `size` is the literal output resolution.
+
+**Audio.** The output MP4 carries the reference video's audio track, as the
+official pipeline does. Set `enable_audio=false` on a request (a `--config` field
+offline, a form field or `extra_body` entry online) for a silent output. If the
+track cannot be decoded, the output is silent and the server logs one warning per
+process; a reference video without an audio track also gives a silent output.
+
+**Lossless conditioning reuse.** Reference-video keys are rotated once and cached per clip, then reused by all
+denoising steps and both CFG branches. This removes repeated RoPE computation
+without changing the attention mask, precision, or sampling schedule. The cache
+uses the existing key storage and is released after the clip; it is not an
+approximate timestep-skipping cache.
+Clips containing only padding that would be removed from the final video are not
+denoised. The padding and conditioning of every retained clip are unchanged.
+
+Text encoding uses the native `TextEncodingStage` and its conditioning cache and
+residency management. CFG-parallel dispatch shares the native CFG utilities while
+retaining the single-GPU arithmetic order.
+Each clip uses the shared denoising loop for step profiling, NVTX ranges, progress,
+and DiT release. Reference K/V preparation and clip-specific prediction remain
+model hooks; clip decoding still feeds the next clip's conditioning. This does
+not enable cache-dit or breakable CUDA graphs for this model.
+Clip decoding uses the shared `DecodingStage.decode_raw` path for VAE compilation,
+tiling and OOM diagnostics. Raw decoded pixels are kept for the next clip: no
+extra conversion to and from `[0, 1]` is introduced. The adapter preserves the
+existing FP32 VAE execution and per-channel latent scaling.
+QKV projections, cross-attention, FFN and the output head are inherited from the
+native Wan implementation. Ulysses exchanges use the shared packed-QKV path;
+the model-specific reference attention mask and K/V lifecycle are retained.
+Text and image conditioning projections are reused within each clip and CFG
+branch, rather than recomputed at every timestep. These projected tensors are
+released after the clip and never reused across requests. Decoded output is
+copied to CPU and clip-local intermediates are released; only the decoded
+overlap frames needed by the next clip remain on the GPU.
+Geometry caches retain at most four RoPE tables and two attention masks, rather
+than accumulating GPU tensors for every request size. Evicted entries are
+recomputed without changing the results; frequently alternating among more
+geometries can add setup work.
+
+Measured on one H200, with a 576×1024 budget, 8 steps, CFG 3, seed 42,
+`clip_len=37`, text-encoder CPU offload, and MP4 plus raw-frame output, the initial
+reuse changes reduced warm request latency from 42.30s to 41.34s (two requests
+per variant). With `clip_len=17`, omitting a fully cropped trailing clip reduced
+59.60s to 40.45s (one warm request per variant). Raw RGB frames were bit-identical
+and peak allocated VRAM did not increase. These are workload-specific results,
+not general speedup claims; both comparisons used PyTorch 2.13.0+cu130,
+Transformers 5.12.1, and Diffusers 0.37.0. The baseline was the initial native
+implementation, not the official Diffusers implementation.
+
+## 2. SGLang-diffusion Installation
+
+SGLang-diffusion offers multiple installation methods. You can choose the most
+suitable installation method based on your hardware platform and requirements.
+
+Please refer to the [official SGLang-diffusion installation guide](/docs/sglang-diffusion/installation)
+for installation instructions.
+
+## 3. Model Deployment
+
+### 3.1 Basic Configuration
+
+On a single high-VRAM GPU, launch the native pipeline with:
+
+```bash Command
+sglang serve \
+  --model-path Wan-AI/Wan2.2-Animate-2-14B-Diffusers \
+  --port 30010
+```
+
+Routing to the native Wan-Animate-2 pipeline is automatic from the checkpoint's
+`model_index.json` (`_class_name: WanAnimate2Pipeline`); pass
+`--pipeline-class-name WanAnimate2Pipeline` only for a local mirror that lacks
+`model_index.json`.
+
+### 3.2 Configuration Tips
+
+See [Performance Optimization](/docs/sglang-diffusion/performance-optimization) for
+acceleration features and their runtime requirements.
+
+- `--num-gpus {NUM_GPUS}`: Number of GPUs to use.
+- `--tp-size {TP_SIZE}`: Tensor parallelism size.
+- `--ulysses-degree {ULYSSES_DEGREE}`: DeepSpeed-Ulysses-style sequence parallelism (USP). The **ring degree must be 1** for this model; `--ring-degree` greater than 1 is rejected with `NotImplementedError`. Combines with `--tp-size`: Ulysses splits the TP-local attention heads, so `--tp-size` must divide the 40 heads and `--ulysses-degree` must divide the per-shard count (see [section 3.3](#3-3-multi-gpu-and-memory-presets)).
+- `--enable-cfg-parallel`: Split the guided and unguided branches across GPUs.
+- `--text-encoder-cpu-offload`: CPU-offload the text encoder to save memory; it is moved to the GPU for the one encode per request.
+
+### 3.3 Multi-GPU and memory presets
+
+| Target | Recommended server flags | Notes |
+| --- | --- | --- |
+| 1 GPU, 96 GB or more | *(no extra flags)* | DiT resident: about 70 GiB peak per GPU at the default workload. Add `--text-encoder-cpu-offload` to keep the fp32 text encoder off the GPU. |
+| 1 GPU, 80 GB | `--dit-layerwise-offload --layerwise-offload-components transformer` | Streams the DiT layer by layer: about 40 GiB peak at the same end-to-end time as the resident DiT; output identical. |
+| 2+ GPUs, long sequences | `--num-gpus N --ulysses-degree N` | Sequence parallel across ranks (ring degree stays 1). |
+| 2+ GPUs, large DiT | `--num-gpus N --tp-size N` | Tensor parallel across attention heads. With `--tp-size` smaller than `--num-gpus` (or than half of it with `--enable-cfg-parallel`), the leftover GPUs are auto-assigned to Ulysses sequence parallelism (last row). |
+| 2 GPUs, split CFG | `--num-gpus 2 --enable-cfg-parallel` | Splits the guided/unguided branches. |
+| 2 GPUs, 80 GB cards | `--num-gpus 2 --enable-cfg-parallel --dit-layerwise-offload --layerwise-offload-components transformer --encoder-parallel replicate --vae-config.use-parallel-decode false` with `SGLANG_DIFFUSION_VAE_CHANNELS_LAST_3D=1` | Same speed as resident CFG-parallel at about 43 GiB per GPU, output bit-identical to a single GPU (the CI configuration). |
+| 4 GPUs | `--num-gpus 4 --enable-cfg-parallel --ulysses-degree 2` | CFG-parallel across two pairs of Ulysses ranks: the fastest 4-GPU layout; pass the flags explicitly to pin the layout instead of relying on the automatic assignment. Ulysses shards the attention sequence, so 4-GPU outputs match the single-GPU video to about 30 dB mean PSNR rather than bit for bit. On 80 GB cards add `--dit-layerwise-offload --layerwise-offload-components transformer` (about 35 GiB per GPU, same speed). |
+| FSDP sharding | `--use-fsdp-inference` is **not supported** | Rejected at startup, before any weights load; use `--tp-size` to shard the DiT or `--dit-layerwise-offload` to cut peak memory. |
+| 4+ GPUs, TP x Ulysses | `--num-gpus 4 --tp-size 2 --ulysses-degree 2` | Tensor parallel across attention heads, Ulysses across the TP-local heads: `--tp-size` must divide the 40 heads and `--ulysses-degree` the per-shard count (`40 / tp`). The memory-leaning 4-GPU layout: about 33 GiB peak per GPU (25 GiB torch reserved), the lowest 4-GPU peak after `--tp-size 4`, at about 13 percent slower than CFG-parallel x tensor parallel and 27 percent slower than the default CFG-parallel x Ulysses layout; use the default for speed and this layout for memory. CFG-parallel can be added on top with twice the GPUs (`--num-gpus 8 --enable-cfg-parallel --tp-size 2 --ulysses-degree 2`). |
+
+## 4. Model Invocation
+
+### 4.1 Generate offline with a config file
+
+The offline path passes both inputs (and the sampling parameters) through a
+`--config` YAML:
+
+```yaml wan_animate_2_run.yaml
+prompt: "a person dancing"
+image_path: /path/to/reference.png
+video_path: /path/to/reference_video.mp4
+clip_len: 37
+height: 800
+width: 640
+num_inference_steps: 40
+guidance_scale: 3.0
+fps: 16
+seed: 42
+```
+
+```bash Command
+sglang generate \
+  --model-path Wan-AI/Wan2.2-Animate-2-14B-Diffusers \
+  --config wan_animate_2_run.yaml \
+  --num-gpus 1 --text-encoder-cpu-offload --pin-cpu-memory \
+  --save-output --output-path outputs --output-file-name wan_animate_2.mp4
+```
+
+Any value in the YAML can also be passed as a CLI flag (for example
+`--image-path`, `--video-path`, `--num-inference-steps`, `--guidance-scale`,
+`--seed`).
+
+### 4.2 Serve and request over HTTP
+
+`POST /v1/videos` creates an asynchronous job. Send the **reference image** as the
+`input_reference` part and the **reference video** as `video_path`, then poll
+the job and download the finished MP4. `size` is the pixel-area budget described in
+[section 1.2](#1-2-defaults); the output dimensions follow the reference image's
+aspect ratio.
+
+```bash Command
+job_id=$(curl -sS -X POST http://127.0.0.1:30010/v1/videos \
+  --form-string "prompt=a person dancing" \
+  --form-string "video_path=/path/to/reference_video.mp4" \
+  --form-string "clip_len=37" \
+  --form-string "size=640x800" \
+  --form-string "num_inference_steps=40" \
+  --form-string "guidance_scale=3.0" \
+  --form-string "fps=16" \
+  --form-string "seed=42" \
+  --form "input_reference=@/path/to/reference.png;type=image/png" \
+  | python -c 'import json, sys; print(json.load(sys.stdin)["id"])')
+
+while true; do
+  status=$(curl -sS "http://127.0.0.1:30010/v1/videos/${job_id}" \
+    | python -c 'import json, sys; print(json.load(sys.stdin)["status"])')
+  [ "$status" = "completed" ] && break
+  [ "$status" = "failed" ] && exit 1
+  sleep 1
+done
+
+curl -sS -L "http://127.0.0.1:30010/v1/videos/${job_id}/content" \
+  -o wan_animate_2.mp4
+```
+
+The same request from the OpenAI Python client. The reference image is the
+`input_reference` file, and `video_path` (a path the server can read) and
+`clip_len` ride `extra_body`:
+
+```python Python
+from openai import OpenAI
+
+client = OpenAI(api_key="EMPTY", base_url="http://127.0.0.1:30010/v1")
+video = client.videos.create(
+    model="Wan-AI/Wan2.2-Animate-2-14B-Diffusers",
+    prompt="a person dancing",
+    input_reference=open("/path/to/reference.png", "rb"),
+    extra_body={
+        "video_path": "/path/to/reference_video.mp4",
+        "clip_len": 37,
+        "guidance_scale": 3.0,
+        "enable_audio": False,  # silent output; the reference video's audio is kept by default
+    },
+)
+```
+
+For more API usage and request examples, see the
+[SGLang Diffusion OpenAI API](/docs/sglang-diffusion/api/openai_api) reference.
+
+### 4.3 Reducing memory
+
+When a single GPU is tight on VRAM, stream the DiT one layer at a time instead of
+resident-loading it:
+
+```bash Command
+sglang serve \
+  --model-path Wan-AI/Wan2.2-Animate-2-14B-Diffusers \
+  --dit-layerwise-offload \
+  --layerwise-offload-components transformer \
+  --port 30010
+```
+
+Combine with `--text-encoder-cpu-offload --pin-cpu-memory` to also keep the text
+encoder off the GPU between uses. Lowering `clip_len` also reduces peak memory.
+

+### 5.1 Native regression coverage
+
+A separate regression used two B300 GPUs, CFG-parallel with replicated encoders
+and serial VAE decode, a 576x1024 area budget, 40 steps, `clip_len=37`, CFG=3,
+and seed 42. The driving input was looped to 64 frames to exercise two clips;
+this is a bounded regression workload, not a long-video quality benchmark.
+Both revisions (`4ee69b4cf9ea` and `04725c1c2900`) used PyTorch 2.14.1+cu130,
+Transformers 5.19.0, Diffusers 0.37.0, and FlashAttention 4.0.0b34 on the same node.
+
+Cold and warm raw RGB outputs were byte-identical to the pre-optimization native
+implementation, both with resident DiT weights and with layerwise DiT offload.
+The single warm samples measured 112.29 s before and 112.40 s after optimization;
+offload measured 113.46 s. This does not establish a significant latency change.
+Rank 0's request-stage peak allocated memory was 52.24, 52.23, and 23.93 GiB,
+respectively; these are not loading peaks or whole-device physical memory peaks.
+
+An H200 HTTP smoke test also covered image upload, asynchronous job polling and
+download, request warmup, repeated requests, URL video input, and reference-audio
+passthrough. Repeated decoded RGB outputs were identical.
+
+These checks preserve the existing native output, not bitwise parity with the
+newer Diffusers modular pipeline. The native sampler follows the original Wan
+sigma grid starting at exactly 1.0 and retains its BF16 conditioning conversion;
+the modular pipeline's sampling and preprocessing differ. Official-reference
+accuracy must be validated separately with pinned versions and aligned settings.
+
+## 6. Troubleshooting
+
+- **OOM**: lower `clip_len` (for example `37` instead of `65`/`81`) or add `--dit-layerwise-offload --layerwise-offload-components transformer`.
+- **`--ring-degree` greater than 1** is rejected at startup with `NotImplementedError`. Use `--ulysses-degree` for sequence parallelism and keep the ring degree at 1.
+- **`--ulysses-degree` that does not divide the TP-local attention heads** (40 / `--tp-size`; with TP 1, degrees 3, 6, 16, ... are rejected) fails at startup with `ValueError`; with TP 1 use 2, 4, 5, 8, 10, 20 or 40. The same check covers leftover GPUs auto-assigned to sequence parallelism (for example `--num-gpus 8 --tp-size 2` runs TP 2 x Ulysses 4).
+- **FSDP** (`--use-fsdp-inference`) is not supported for this model and is rejected at startup; use `--tp-size` or DiT layerwise offload for memory.
+- **`--attention-backend`** (or `--component-attention-backends transformer=...`) is rejected at startup with `ValueError`: the in-context self-attention runs on torch `flex_attention` only. The text encoder still accepts `--component-attention-backends text_encoder=<backend>`.
+- **`enable_teacache` / `enable_spectrum`** request fields are rejected with `ValueError`: every block runs at every step, so the cache heuristics do not apply.
+- **`SGLANG_DIFFUSION_ENABLE_MXFP8_ATTENTION`** is rejected at startup with `ValueError`: this model does not apply the offline Q/K rotation.
+- **Silent output**: the reference video's audio track is kept only when it can be decoded; otherwise the output is silent and the server logs one warning per process naming the cause. A reference video without an audio track also gives a silent output (one info line). Pass `enable_audio=false` to skip audio extraction altogether.
+- **Reference video not found**: `video_path` must be a path the server process can read. Pass it as `--video-path` or through `--config` offline, or in the request body online.

+from dataclasses import dataclass, field
+
+from sglang.multimodal_gen.configs.models.dits.base import DiTConfig
+from sglang.multimodal_gen.configs.models.dits.wanvideo import WanVideoArchConfig
+
+# Checkpoint block params use the official Wan names nested under `blocks.{i}.block.*`.
+# The loader applies mapping rules in insertion order, re-scanning after each hit, so the
+# extras below chain into the reused Wan lora (official -> hf) and main (hf -> native) maps.
+_WAN = WanVideoArchConfig()
+
+
+_WAN_ANIMATE_2_EXTRA_MAPPING: dict[str, str] = {
+    # Strip the `.block` infix so the reused Wan rules match.
+    r"^blocks\.(\d+)\.block\.(.*)$": r"blocks.\1.\2",
+    # Self-attn / cross-attn qk-norms (not covered by the Wan lora map).
+    r"^blocks\.(\d+)\.self_attn\.norm_q\.(.*)$": r"blocks.\1.norm_q.\2",
+    r"^blocks\.(\d+)\.self_attn\.norm_k\.(.*)$": r"blocks.\1.norm_k.\2",
+    r"^blocks\.(\d+)\.cross_attn\.norm_q\.(.*)$": r"blocks.\1.attn2.norm_q.\2",
+    r"^blocks\.(\d+)\.cross_attn\.norm_k\.(.*)$": r"blocks.\1.attn2.norm_k.\2",
+    # Cross-attn I2V image branch -> WanI2VCrossAttention add_k_proj/add_v_proj/norm_added_k.
+    r"^blocks\.(\d+)\.cross_attn\.k_img\.(.*)$": r"blocks.\1.attn2.add_k_proj.\2",
+    r"^blocks\.(\d+)\.cross_attn\.v_img\.(.*)$": r"blocks.\1.attn2.add_v_proj.\2",
+    r"^blocks\.(\d+)\.cross_attn\.norm_k_img\.(.*)$": r"blocks.\1.attn2.norm_added_k.\2",
+    # The Diffusers checkpoint keeps the official self_attn/cross_attn prefixes but names
+    # the projections the diffusers way (to_q/to_k/to_v/to_out.0, add_*_proj).
+    r"^blocks\.(\d+)\.self_attn\.to_out\.0\.(.*)$": r"blocks.\1.to_out.\2",
+    r"^blocks\.(\d+)\.self_attn\.(to_q|to_k|to_v)\.(.*)$": r"blocks.\1.\2.\3",
+    r"^blocks\.(\d+)\.cross_attn\.to_out\.0\.(.*)$": r"blocks.\1.attn2.to_out.\2",
+    r"^blocks\.(\d+)\.cross_attn\.(to_q|to_k|to_v|add_k_proj|add_v_proj|norm_added_k)\.(.*)$": r"blocks.\1.attn2.\2.\3",
+    # `norm3` is the block's only affine LayerNorm and feeds cross-attn; the reused rules
+    # only know its hf name (`norm2`).
+    r"^blocks\.(\d+)\.norm3\.(.*)$": r"blocks.\1.self_attn_residual_norm.norm.\2",
+    # Per-block 6-way modulation -> scale_shift_table.
+    r"^blocks\.(\d+)\.modulation$": r"blocks.\1.scale_shift_table",

+    r"^head\.head\.(.*)$": r"proj_out.\1",
+    r"^head\.modulation$": r"scale_shift_table",
+    r"^head\.norm\.(.*)$": r"norm_out.\1",

+    r"^text_embedding\.0\.(.*)$": r"condition_embedder.text_embedder.fc_in.\1",

+    def _rope_tables(
+        self,
+        f_range: tuple[int, int, int],  # (start, length, stride)
+        h_range: tuple[int, int],  # (start, length)
+        w_range: tuple[int, int],
+    ) -> tuple[torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor]:

+        The table is cached per ranges."""

+            self._rope_cache.move_to_end(key)

+        w_idx = torch.arange(w_range[1], device=self._device) + w_range[0]

+        # the in-context blocks all-to-all-gather the full sequence before applying RoPE.
+        ff, hh, ww = torch.meshgrid(f_idx, h_idx, w_idx, indexing="ij")

+        return self._rope_tables((0, f, 1), (0, h), (0, w))

+    def _reference_video_rope(
+        self, f: int, h: int, w: int, generation_video_w: int
+    ) -> tuple[torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor]:

+    @torch.no_grad()

+    def forward(

+        encoder_hidden_states: torch.Tensor,  # this CFG branch's prompt embeddings [L, C]
+        timestep: torch.Tensor,  # [1]

+        reference_kv: WanAnimate2ReferenceKV,
+        # This clip's conditioning from build_clip_conditioning.
+        clip_cond: WanAnimate2ClipConditioning,

+            projected_context

+                encoder_hidden_states, encoder_hidden_states_image
+            )
+        )
+        layout = _InContextLayout(
+            (f, h, w),
+            clip_cond.reference_video_grid_sizes,
+            clip_cond.full_clip_grid_sizes,
+        )
+
+        # No seq padding here: hidden_states is exactly f*h*w tokens and the in-context
+        # layout pads internally. Under Ulysses SP each block a2a-gathers the full
+        # sequence, so shard tail padding lands at the global tail where forward_gen
+        # expects it.
+        if sp_size > 1:
+            hidden_states, _ = shard_seq(hidden_states, dim=1)
+        hidden_states = self._run_generation_blocks(
+            hidden_states,
+            encoder_hidden_states=generation_encoder_hidden_states,
+            timestep_modulation=timestep_modulation,

+    def _make_generation_input(

+        """36-channel DiT input ``[1, 36, f, h, w]``: the fp32 noisy latent over the bf16 generation condition."""
+        # Both cast to the param dtype so the cat runs in bf16 and does not rely on autocast;
+        # the fp32 latent would be rounded to bf16 by the patch embedding anyway.
+        return torch.cat(
+            [latent.to(self._dtype), generation_condition.to(self._dtype)], dim=0

+    def _run_generation_blocks(
+        self,
+        hidden_states: torch.Tensor,
+        *,

+        timestep_modulation: torch.Tensor,

+        reference_kv: WanAnimate2ReferenceKV,

+                layout.generation_video_h,
+                layout.generation_video_w,

+            # Block 9 is dropped on the unconditional branch, as in the reference
+            # wan_animate_2_model.forward_gen; the authors give no rationale.
+            if is_unconditional and idx == 9:

+                kv_cache_mode="gen",
+                hidden_states=hidden_states,
+                encoder_hidden_states=encoder_hidden_states,
+                timestep_modulation=timestep_modulation,
+                gen_cos=generation_video_rope_cos,
+                gen_sin=generation_video_rope_sin,
+                block_mask=block_mask,
+                layout=layout,
+                index=idx,
+                k_cache=reference_kv.k,
+                v_cache=reference_kv.v,
+            )

+#
+# Wan-Animate-2 DiT block: in-context self-attention over [gen tokens, then cached
+# reference-video K/V], its RoPE / Ulysses helpers, and the per-clip _InContextLayout
+# geometry.
+# Names kept from the reference implementation: the forward_ref / forward_gen methods and the
+# kv_cache_mode values "ref" / "gen"; there "ref" means the reference video (the motion source), not the reference image.
+from __future__ import annotations

+import math
+from collections.abc import Callable
+from functools import lru_cache, partial
+from typing import Any, Literal

+import torch
+from torch.nn.attention.flex_attention import BlockMask, flex_attention

+from sglang.multimodal_gen.runtime.distributed import (
+    get_sp_world_size,
+)
+from sglang.multimodal_gen.runtime.layers.usp import (
+    _usp_input_all_to_all_qkv as _sp_gather_qkv,
+)
+from sglang.multimodal_gen.runtime.layers.usp import (
+    _usp_output_all_to_all,
+)
+from sglang.multimodal_gen.runtime.models.dits.wanvideo import WanTransformerBlock
+
+# Eager flex_attention materializes the full [Q, KV] scores over the padded [gen | reference-video]
+# sequence (tens of GiB at video resolution); compiled, it is one fused kernel.
+_flex_attention_compiled = torch.compile(
+    flex_attention,
+    dynamic=False,
+    mode="max-autotune",
+    fullgraph=True,
+    backend="inductor",
+)
+
+
+def _apply_rope_interleaved(
+    x: torch.Tensor, cos: torch.Tensor, sin: torch.Tensor
+) -> torch.Tensor:
+    """Interleaved (GPT-J style) RoPE, identical to ``_apply_rotary_emb(is_neox_style=False)``;
+    ``x`` is ``[B, S, H, D]``, ``cos`` / ``sin`` are ``[S, D//2]`` fp32."""
+    cos = cos[None, :, None, :]  # [1, S, 1, D//2]
+    sin = sin[None, :, None, :]
+    x1 = x[..., 0::2].float()
+    x2 = x[..., 1::2].float()
+    o1 = x1 * cos - x2 * sin
+    o2 = x2 * cos + x1 * sin
+    out = torch.stack([o1, o2], dim=-1).flatten(-2)
+    return out.type_as(x)
+
+
+def _score_mod_impl(
+    score: torch.Tensor,
+    b_idx: torch.Tensor,
+    h_idx: torch.Tensor,
+    q_idx: torch.Tensor,
+    kv_idx: torch.Tensor,
+    hw: int,
+    log_scale: float,
+) -> torch.Tensor:
+    # Biases the keys of generation frame 1, [hw, 2*hw) in the padded layout, exactly as the
+    # official Wan-Animate-2 code does; non-zero only when the checkpoint config sets log_scale.
+    condition = (kv_idx >= hw) & (kv_idx < 2 * hw)
+    return torch.where(condition, score + log_scale, score)
+
+
+@lru_cache(maxsize=None)
+def _make_score_mod(hw: int, log_scale: float) -> Callable[..., torch.Tensor]:
+    # Stable object identity per (hw, log_scale): compiled flex_attention guards on the
+    # score_mod object, so a fresh closure per call would recompile every clip.
+    return partial(_score_mod_impl, hw=hw, log_scale=log_scale)
+
+
+def _sp_scatter_out(attn_output: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
+    """Ulysses output a2a: [B, S_full, N_local, C] -> [B, S_local, N_tp, C]."""
+    return _usp_output_all_to_all(attn_output, head_dim=2)
+
+
+def _reference_video_key_mask(
+    *, batch_size: int, seq_len: int, num_valid: int, device: torch.device
+) -> torch.Tensor:
+    """``[B, S]`` bool key mask: True for the leading ``num_valid`` reference-video tokens."""
+    key_mask = torch.zeros((batch_size, seq_len), dtype=torch.bool, device=device)
+    key_mask[:, :num_valid] = True
+    return key_mask

+
+class WanAnimate2TransformerBlock(WanTransformerBlock):
+    """Wan block with the Wan-Animate-2 in-context self-attention.
+
+    No new parameters: forward_ref / forward_gen reuse the inherited modules and only
+    route the self-attention differently.

+    def __init__(self, *args: Any, log_scale: float = 0.0, **kwargs: Any) -> None:

+            )

+    def _modulate(
+        self, timestep_modulation: torch.Tensor
+    ) -> tuple[
+        torch.Tensor,
+        torch.Tensor,
+        torch.Tensor,
+        torch.Tensor,
+        torch.Tensor,
+        torch.Tensor,

+class _InContextLayout:
+    """Token geometry of the padded [generation | reference-video] in-context layout.
+
+    Three sets of sizes: this clip's token counts; those of a full-length clip, which every
+    clip is padded up to; and the full-length sizes rounded up to 128 for flex_attention.
+    The attention pads to the last set and the block mask is built from the same numbers,
+    so one compiled mask serves every clip of a request."""

+    def __init__(

+        generation_video_grid: tuple[int, int, int],
+        reference_video_grid: tuple[int, int, int],
+        full_clip_grid: tuple[int, int, int],
+    ) -> None:
+        f, h, w = generation_video_grid
+        reference_video_f, reference_video_h, reference_video_w = reference_video_grid
+        full_clip_f, full_clip_h, full_clip_w = full_clip_grid
+        self.generation_video_f, self.generation_video_h, self.generation_video_w = (
+            f,
+            h,
+            w,
+        )
+        self.reference_video_f, self.reference_video_h, self.reference_video_w = (
+            reference_video_f,
+            reference_video_h,
+            reference_video_w,
+        )
+
+        # This clip; shorter than full length only for the last clip of a video.
+        self.generation_video_tokens_per_frame = h * w
+        self.reference_video_tokens_per_frame = reference_video_h * reference_video_w
+        self.generation_video_num_tokens = f * h * w
+        self.reference_video_num_tokens = (
+            reference_video_f * reference_video_h * reference_video_w
+        )
+

+        # the reference video does not.

+        self.max_generation_video_num_tokens = full_clip_f * self.max_tokens_per_frame
+        self.max_reference_video_num_tokens = (
+            full_clip_f - 1
+        ) * self.max_tokens_per_frame

+            math.ceil(self.max_generation_video_num_tokens / 128) * 128

+            math.ceil(self.max_reference_video_num_tokens / 128) * 128

+        """Returns the block mask function based on the [gen | reference-video] in-context layout.
+
+        A valid gen query attends every valid gen key plus the reference-video keys of its own frame.
+
+        keys:     [generation tokens | generation pad | reference tokens | reference pad]
